subject: Geography
description: Domain-specific trap patterns for UPSC Prelims Geomorphology questions. Based on PYQ analysis (2015-2024, 30 questions). Maps question types to trap patterns with generation rules. Uses base patterns from traps_geography_base.json with Geomorphology-specific variations and new patterns unique to this domain.

assertion_reason.description: Statement A is given; Reason R is given. Evaluate if A is true, R is true, and if R explains A. MOST COMMON in Geomorphology (40% vs 15% overall Geography)
assertion_reason.characteristics: Tests cause-effect and logical linkage. Geomorphology emphasizes process chains and mechanism understanding.

trap_patterns.name: Direction/Scale reversal in process explanation
trap_patterns.mechanism: Assertion correct, but reason reverses direction/scale. E.g., 'Meanders form BECAUSE low gradient allows lateral erosion' (correct) vs 'Meanders form because HIGH gradient increases lateral erosion' (reversed scale direction)
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use correct concept but reverse the qualifying direction (upstream/downstream, leeward/windward, high/low)
trap_patterns.example: A: Meanders are prominent in plains. R: Because gradient is HIGH, lateral erosion dominates. [WRONG: gradient is LOW]
generation_rules: Assert a correct geomorphic observation
Provide reason that is mechanistically correct but directionally reversed
Reverse one key qualifier: gradient (high↔low), direction (upstream↔downstream, north↔south), location (leeward↔windward)
Student recognizes concept but gets direction wrong due to reading speed

trap_patterns.name: Process chain skip (missing intermediate step)
trap_patterns.mechanism: Assertion true, reason incomplete or skips key step. E.g., 'Fjords have U-shaped valleys. Reason: Because they were carved by glaciers.' [TRUE but incomplete: glaciers → ice flow → downward + lateral erosion → U-shape]
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Correct starting and ending points, but skip or shortcut the intermediate process steps
trap_patterns.example: A: U-shaped valleys are found in mountain regions. R: Because mountains have steep slopes. [WRONG: Missing the glacier erosion mechanism]
generation_rules: Assert a correct geomorphic outcome
Provide reason that identifies a correct trigger but omits intermediate steps
Use statements that seem plausible because they're partially correct
Hard questions specifically test if students understand FULL process chains, not just endpoints

trap_patterns.name: Counterintuitive fact in reason (tropical vs polar)
trap_patterns.mechanism: A true, R true, but R counterintuitive (tropical weathering faster than polar). Student rejects correct reason because it violates prior belief.
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: State counterintuitive mechanism as true reason. Student's intuitive but incorrect answer (freeze-thaw is dominant) available as distractor.
trap_patterns.example: A: Tropical soils are deeper than polar soils. R: Because tropical regions have higher chemical weathering rates despite lower freeze-thaw cycles.
generation_rules: Assert a true observation about tropical vs other regions
Provide counterintuitive reason (tropical weathering > polar)
Make student's intuitive answer (freeze-thaw dominates) available as option
Use in hard questions (A/R + counterintuitive + process understanding)

trap_patterns.name: Both A and R true, but causally disconnected
trap_patterns.mechanism: Both assertion and reason are factually correct, but R doesn't explain A. Student mistakes correlation for causation.
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Both seem related but actually independent; student assumes causal linkage
trap_patterns.example: A: Laterite soils are found in tropical regions. R: Because tropical regions receive high rainfall. [TRUE but not causal: laterization requires DRAINAGE + weathering + climate, not just rainfall]
generation_rules: Assert a true fact
Provide a true but causally unrelated fact
Both must seem plausible as related concepts
Test whether student confuses correlation with causation

trap_patterns.name: Scale ambiguity in assertions
trap_patterns.mechanism: Assertion mixes scales (local meanders with regional drainage). Reason is true for one scale but not the other.
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use correct mechanism but at wrong scale (local vs regional, temporal vs spatial)
trap_patterns.example: A: River patterns are determined by climate. R: Because monsoon rainfall varies seasonally. [WRONG: Pattern formation = long-term, not seasonal variation]
generation_rules: Mix temporal or spatial scales in assertion
Reason is correct for one scale but not the other
Student must distinguish local vs regional, seasonal vs decadal

multi_statement.description: 2-3 statements; evaluate which are correct using given options. Second most common in Geomorphology (35% vs 25% overall Geography).
multi_statement.characteristics: Options guide answer; allows strategic partial elimination. Tests concept combinations and process understanding.

trap_patterns.name: Partial truth distractors (correct on one dimension, incomplete on another)
trap_patterns.mechanism: Statement is partially true: correct concept but incomplete driver. E.g., 'Freeze-thaw dominates in high mountains' vs 'Freeze-thaw dominates in alpine zones' (missing: only where water-saturated).
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use correct concept but incomplete condition or location qualifier
trap_patterns.example: Stmt 1: 'Laterite forms in tropical regions.' [Partially true: forms in DRAINED tropical regions] Stmt 2: 'Weathering rate is highest in tropical regions.' [TRUE] Answer: Only statement 2
generation_rules: State a geomorphic process correctly but incompletely
Include correct location/climate but miss the enabling condition (drainage, slope, vegetation)
Use in medium difficulty: students know concept but miss nuance

trap_patterns.name: Similar landforms confusion (match concept to correct feature)
trap_patterns.mechanism: Two statements describe similar-looking landforms but with different erosional agents. E.g., 'Drumlins are glacier-shaped ridges' vs 'Moraines are glacier-deposited ridges' (students confuse due to similar appearance).
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use related but distinct concepts; differentiate by process or origin
trap_patterns.example: Stmt 1: 'U-shaped valleys form by glacial erosion.' [TRUE] Stmt 2: 'V-shaped valleys form by river erosion.' [TRUE] Stmt 3: 'Fjords are U-shaped valleys that were submerged.' [TRUE] Answer: All three
generation_rules: Include multiple similar-looking landforms in one question
Test whether student knows the DISTINCT process creating each
Use matching strategy: pair each landform with correct erosional agent

trap_patterns.name: Climate linkage confusion (which climate produces which landform)
trap_patterns.mechanism: Statements about landforms conditioned on climate. Student may know the landform but misattribute to wrong climate. E.g., 'Barchan dunes form in hot deserts' (TRUE) vs 'Barchan dunes form in cold deserts' (FALSE).
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Reverse climate condition (hot↔cold, wet↔dry, high altitude↔low altitude)
trap_patterns.example: Stmt 1: 'Laterite soils form in wet tropical regions with good drainage.' [TRUE] Stmt 2: 'Laterite soils form in dry tropical regions.' [FALSE] Stmt 3: 'Laterite soils are hardened in place.' [TRUE]
generation_rules: State geomorphic processes with climate conditions
Reverse one climatic variable for false statement
Use in medium questions where student knows landform but misses climate condition

trap_patterns.name: Process sequence reversal (which step comes first)
trap_patterns.mechanism: Statements about process steps but in wrong sequence. E.g., 'Meanders form THEN gradients decrease' vs 'Gradients decrease THEN meanders form' (causality matters).
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Reverse the temporal/causal sequence of process steps
trap_patterns.example: Stmt 1: 'River headward erosion captures a tributary.' [correct] Stmt 2: 'Wind and water gaps form BEFORE river capture occurs.' [FALSE: they form AS A RESULT OF capture] Answer: Only statement 1
generation_rules: State geomorphic processes with causal sequencing
Reverse the order of cause → effect in false statements
Use in hard questions where students know concepts but miss causality

match_pair.description: Match entities (landforms, features, locations); 3-4 pairs given, evaluate how many are correctly matched. Third most common in Geomorphology (15% vs 14% overall Geography). Tests precision knowledge of landform locations and characteristics.
match_pair.characteristics: Requires one-to-one mapping; precision in definitions essential. Geomorphology emphasizes spatial/location precision.

trap_patterns.name: Correct concept, wrong geographic detail (location mismatch)
trap_patterns.mechanism: Landform is correctly identified but paired with wrong location/feature. E.g., 'Kanyakumari has cliffs' (correct) vs 'Kanyakumari has sandy beaches' (incorrect; it's rocky).
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use real landform and real location but incorrect pairing
trap_patterns.example: Pair 1: 'Sundarbans - mangrove swamps' [CORRECT] Pair 2: 'Sundarbans - sandy beaches' [WRONG: mangrove-dominated] Pair 3: 'Thar Desert - sand dunes' [CORRECT]
generation_rules: Match landforms to specific Indian/global locations
One pair: correct concept, wrong location (but real location with different feature)
Requires map knowledge and spatial precision

trap_patterns.name: Similar landforms, wrong agent pairing
trap_patterns.mechanism: Landform correctly identified but paired with wrong erosional agent. E.g., 'U-shaped valley - fluvial erosion' (WRONG: glacial erosion).
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use correct landform but wrong process/agent; both are plausible
trap_patterns.example: Pair 1: 'Drumlins - glacier flow direction indicator' [CORRECT] Pair 2: 'Drumlins - wind erosion' [WRONG: glacial, not wind] Pair 3: 'Barchan - wind-shaped sand dune' [CORRECT]
generation_rules: Match landforms to erosional agents/processes
One pair: landform correct, but agent is plausibly wrong
Test whether students know which PROCESS creates which form

trap_patterns.name: Synonym confusion (different terms, same concept)
trap_patterns.mechanism: Student confuses synonymous terms or near-synonyms. E.g., 'Fjord' vs 'Ria' (both are drowned valleys but different origins).
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use similar terms or synonyms; require distinction by origin/process
trap_patterns.example: Pair 1: 'Fjord - glacially carved drowned valley' [CORRECT] Pair 2: 'Ria - glacially carved drowned valley' [WRONG: ria is fluvially carved, not glacial]
generation_rules: Use confusable landform terms (fjord/ria, drumlin/moraine, meander/oxbow)
Require students to distinguish by process or origin, not just appearance
One pair mixes up similar concepts

direct_fact.description: Single fact question; one correct answer from 4 options. Least common in Geomorphology (10% vs 18% overall Geography). Often tests definition or pure CA.
direct_fact.characteristics: Minimal inference required; tests recall and precision. Geomorphology emphasizes definitions and terminology over pure geography facts.

trap_patterns.name: Definition precision (synonym vs strict definition)
trap_patterns.mechanism: Question asks for definition; student picks synonym instead of precise definition. E.g., 'What is a drumlin? A) elongated ridge B) glacier-shaped ridge from subglacial flow C) mound of glacial sediment D) ice-sculpted hill'.
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use related but less specific or incorrect definitions as distractors
trap_patterns.example: Q: 'Which of the following best describes a drumlin?' A) 'An elongated ridge shaped by glacial flow' [CORRECT] B) 'A mound of glacial sediment' [LESS PRECISE] C) 'A ridge formed by glacial meltwater' [WRONG] D) 'A U-shaped valley carved by ice' [WRONG]
generation_rules: Ask for precise definition of geomorphic feature
Include similar but less precise definitions as distractors
Require knowledge of process/origin, not just appearance

trap_patterns.name: CA-triggered landslide/flood recognition
trap_patterns.mechanism: Recent event (landslide, flood, erosion) mentioned; student must identify the geomorphic process. E.g., '2024 Himachal Pradesh landslides are caused by... A) Slope instability + freeze-thaw + deforestation B) Heavy rainfall C) Plate tectonics D) Wind erosion'.
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use simpler but incorrect processes; make student focus on news rather than process
trap_patterns.example: Recent Brahmaputra channel shifts in Assam are caused by: A) River piracy and channel migration B) Seasonal flooding C) Glacier melt D) Erosion [CORRECT: A, involves complex channel dynamics, not just flooding]
generation_rules: Use recent landslide, flood, or erosion event from news
Question tests geomorphic process, not just CA knowledge
Distractors: simpler processes (rainfall, flooding) that students might assume

trap_patterns.name: Scale/scope confusion (local vs regional)
trap_patterns.mechanism: Question about scale of geomorphic feature. E.g., 'Meanders are features of: A) Small streams B) Low-gradient plains C) Both A and B in different contexts D) High mountain valleys'.
trap_patterns.distractor_strategy: Use correct feature but wrong scale
trap_patterns.example: Q: 'Where are sand dunes MOST extensive? A) Thar Desert B) Coastal regions C) River floodplains D) Foothills'
generation_rules: Ask about scale or geographic scope of landform
Test whether student knows typical occurrence context
Distractors: other plausible but wrong locations

trap_patterns_global_mapping.description: How Geomorphology-specific traps map to base trap patterns from traps_geography_base.json

mapping.GEO_AR_T01 (Direction reversal): Maps to pattern_6 (Spatial sequence reversal) + pattern_2 (embedded precision error)
mapping.GEO_AR_T02 (Process chain skip): New pattern (unique to Geomorphology) — tests sequential reasoning
mapping.GEO_AR_T03 (Counterintuitive): Maps to pattern_1 (Reverse the obvious) — tropical vs polar
mapping.GEO_AR_T04 (Logical disconnection): Maps to pattern_2_ar_variant (Both A and R true, but not linked)
mapping.GEO_AR_T05 (Scale ambiguity): New pattern (emerging in recent years) — local vs regional confusion
mapping.GEO_MS_T03 (Climate linkage): Maps to pattern_3 (Statistical precision reversal) — climate reversal variant
mapping.GEO_MS_T04 (Process sequence): New pattern (unique to Geomorphology) — causality and temporal ordering
mapping.GEO_MP_T01 (Location mismatch): Maps to pattern_4 (Adjacent fact confusion) — concept right, location wrong
mapping.GEO_MP_T02 (Wrong agent): Maps to pattern_4 (Adjacent fact confusion) — landform right, process wrong
mapping.GEO_MP_T03 (Synonym confusion): Maps to pattern_4 (Adjacent fact confusion) — similar terms, different origins
mapping.GEO_DF_T01 (Definition precision): Maps to pattern_5 (CA trigger) — terminology testing
mapping.GEO_DF_T02 (CA-triggered): Maps to pattern_5 (CA trigger on static fact)
mapping.GEO_DF_T03 (Scale/scope): New pattern — geographic distribution of landforms

unique_patterns_in_geomorphology: GEO_AR_T02: Process chain skip — not prominent in other subjects
GEO_AR_T05: Scale ambiguity — specific to spatial reasoning domains
GEO_MS_T04: Process sequence reversal — unique causality testing
GEO_DF_T03: Scale/scope confusion — emerging pattern, not in other subjects
notes: Geomorphology traps emphasize spatial reasoning (direction, location, 3D visualization) over other subjects
Process chains are critical: students must understand A→B→C sequences, not just individual concepts
Scale confusion (local vs regional, temporal vs spatial) is a unique challenge in Geomorphology
Assertion-Reason format (40% in Geomorphology vs 15% overall) requires understanding of causality and mechanism
Similar-looking landforms (drumlins/moraines, fjord/ria, meanders/oxbows) are common traps
CA integration emerging: floods/landslides/channel shifts tied to geomorphic processes, not just events
